Sheeran’s Loop Tour was the highest-grossing in the world, with an average box office gross of over $7 million (€6m) per city, Pollstar said in May. Through the end of 2025, Sheeran was the third-highest earning concert act since 2021.
Sheeran has said the tour promoter was ultimately responsible for the decision to drop Macklemore.

He also said he “spoke with the venues at length all week to try to build a bridge” before Macklemore was dropped. He insisted he would never willingly let down his fans or abandon the touring crew and others who rely on him to make a living.
While promoters and venues wield great power over concert tours, experts say an artist of Sheeran's magnitude generally has the final say about what happens concerning the shows.

Vice Premier He Lifeng, China's top negotiator for trade, will visit the United States for talks ahead of a summit between presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, state media said on Saturday.
The leaders of the world's two biggest economies are due to meet at the White House on September 24 in a bid to ease tensions over trade, technology and broader strategic issues.

Trade relations will top the agenda

But trade issues are expected to take centre stage when Xi and Trump meet.
The world's two largest economies reached a fragile truce in October 2025 after months of tariff tensions triggered by Trump following his return to the White House.
The agreement helped cool fears of a damaging trade escalation, but negotiators on both sides have yet to reach a comprehensive settlement, leaving key disputes unresolved.

North Korea reveals new drone production lines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:50:08 UTC
16:50:08 KST

- North Korean state media showed Kim Jong Un touring drone production lines Sept. 16-18, including a one-way attack drone resembling Israeli loitering munitions.
- The drone's launcher system first appeared publicly at an October 2025 military parade, mounted six per truck on four vehicles.
North Korean state media revealed production lines for at least three types of domestically built drones this week, including a one-way attack drone that resembles Israeli-designed loitering munitions, as part of a factory tour by leader Kim Jong Un reported Sept. 19.
The ruling Workers’ Party newspaper Rodong Sinmun said Kim, the party’s general secretary, inspected “important munitions industry enterprises” from Sept. 16 to 18. Photos accompanying the report showed him walking through an assembly hall containing dozens of small flying-wing drones mounted on stands, alongside separate images of him examining what appeared to be missile or drone airframe components with factory officials.
One drone shown is a one-way attack type visually similar to Israel’s Harop family of loitering munitions, weapons built to fly toward a target and detonate on impact rather than return to base. North Korea unveiled a dedicated launch system for this drone at a nighttime military parade on Oct. 10, 2025, marking the Workers’ Party’s 80th anniversary.
That parade featured four 6×6 trucks, each carrying two stacked rows of three launch containers, for an apparent capacity of six drones per vehicle. The parade followed an August 2024 reveal of prototype airframes styled after Israel’s Harop and Switchblade-style “Hero” loitering munitions, neither of which came with published performance figures at the time.
This week’s images of the attack drone during testing were partly obscured, withholding a clear view of some components, though analysts have suggested the design may be related to a rail-launched drone North Korea has separately tested that uses a small rocket booster to get airborne.
Other drones shown on the factory floor were still semi-complete airframes, but their shape already matched North Korea’s larger reconnaissance-strike drones, the Saetbyol-4 and Saetbyol-9.
Both first appeared publicly in July 2023 and have undergone repeated flight tests since. The Saetbyol-4 bears a resemblance to the U.S. RQ-4 Global Hawk surveillance drone, while the Saetbyol-9, with a wingspan of roughly 20 meters (66 feet), resembles the U.S. MQ-9 Reaper and carries hardpoints that suggest it is built to fire guided weapons rather than only observe. North Korean state media has separately called for expanded production across the country’s drone programs, following Kim’s public push earlier this year to accelerate output.
The factory visit came the same week Kim toured facilities producing a mobile rocket launcher that outside analysts have compared to the U.S. Army’s HIMARS system, and the same week North Korea rejected an International Atomic Energy Agency resolution criticizing its nuclear weapons program.
North Korea has not disclosed the factory locations, production quantities for any of the drones shown, or further technical detail on the attack drone beyond what appears in the partly obscured photos.

China railway passenger trips hit record high in first eight months
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
15:49:57 CST
16:49:57 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 19 (Xinhua) -- China handled a record 3.32 billion railway passenger trips in the first eight months of 2026, up 3.9 percent year on year, according to the China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway).
During the period, the railway network operated an average of 11,508 passenger trains daily, up 5 percent from a year earlier.
Responding to passenger growth driven by the country's transit visa-free policy, the railway network recorded over 16.68 million foreign passenger trips in the first eight months, up 33.3 percent year on year.
Cross-border rail travel also continued to grow. The China-Laos Railway carried 245,000 cross-border trips, up 39.1 percent, while the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed railway handled over 23.4 million cross-border trips, up 10.7 percent, China Railway said.
Analysts attributed the record to the expansion of China's high-speed rail network, stronger operational capacity, a rebound in tourism consumption and easier cross-border travel.
China has expanded its 240-hour visa-free transit program to 57 countries, with Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam the latest added. The policy has helped fuel a surge in cross-border travel, with Chinese border authorities handling 499 million inbound and outbound trips in the first eight months, up 8.7 percent year on year.
China Railway has also worked with local cultural and tourism departments to promote tourism, operating 2,501 tourist trains nationwide during the period.
Aboard the Y839 tourist train from Xining to Lhasa, Chris, a 56-year-old British tourist, was traveling to China with his wife and daughter for the first time, with Lhasa as the first stop. Long fascinated by China, he chose the train to take in the plateau scenery. "This train is carrying more than 30 foreign passengers from seven countries, including Thailand, Britain and Japan," said Gai Mingjing, conductor of the Y839 train.
China Railway said it will prepare for the upcoming Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday travel rush, improve station and onboard services, and run distinctive tourist trains to give passengers a better travel experience. ■

An aerial drone photo taken on Aug. 11, 2026 shows a view of the Xiangjiang River in Quanzhou County of Guilin City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. In the winter of 1934 during the Long March, the Red Army fought its way across the Xiangjiang River in Guangxi and broke through the Kuomintang troops' blockade, but suffered tens of thousands of casualties in the battle.
In Quanzhou, Guanyang and Xing'an counties, where the Battle of the Xiangjiang River was fought, the spirit of the Long March has been passed down through generations. Today, roads wind through mountains that Red Army soldiers once crossed on foot, connecting once-isolated villages with the outside world. BEIJING, Sept. 19 (Xinhua) -- China will strengthen its cultural industries and tourism over the next five years, aiming to steadily raise their share of GDP, according to the Ministry of Culture and Tourism.
The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural and tourism development, newly released by the ministry, calls for turning the sectors into pillars of economic development and businesses that improve people's livelihoods and sense of happiness.
One key target is 8.3 billion domestic trips a year by 2030, nearly 2 billion more than in 2025.
Chinese tourists spent 6.3 trillion yuan (about 933 billion U.S. dollars) on domestic trips in 2025. The 2030 target is 7.7 trillion yuan.
Market analysis shows tourism spending is increasingly flowing into sectors that blend culture and new experiences into travel.
Traveling for concerts, sports events and commercial performances, or to explore places known for revolutionary history or modern industry, is a notable example.
"It all points to the same trend: tourists are no longer satisfied with a tour that is just about moving from one place to another, but a trip that can invoke cultural identity, or enable them to express their identity or experience something new," said a report by Meadin Research Institute, a market analytics firm.
Such an infusion represents a focus of efforts to boost cultural industry and tourism in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural and tourism development.
The plan supports industrial tourism based on equipment manufacturing and consumer goods, travel packages featuring farming experiences, and comprehensive consumption scenarios.
Other efforts include further integrating sports events with cultural tourism, fostering high-quality ski destinations and promoting deeper links between cultural tourism and transportation.
For 2030, the plan pledges to create diverse, immersive and interactive consumption scenarios, while boosting spending on cruise and yacht tours and recreational vehicle camping.
To cultivate tour packages and business models that integrate culture and tourism, the plan says revolutionary culture and fine traditional Chinese culture can be used to build an emotional connection and improve the tourist experience.
It also encourages employers to ensure paid vacation and stagger holidays to boost tourism spending.
GROWING APPEAL FOR INTERNATIONAL TOURISTS
Improving tourist experience in China appeals to both domestic and international visitors, especially with continued support expected over the next five years.
The World Tourism Cities Federation (WTCF) listed Beijing, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Hangzhou and Chengdu among the world's top 20 tourist cities in its latest World Tourism Cities Development Report (2025-2026).
China has the most cities on the list, according to the report released at a sideline event during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, held in Beijing from Sept. 9 to 13.
Joseph Lema, an expert with the WTCF, said competition among tourism cities has moved beyond attractions and visitor numbers. What matters now, he said, is the ability to deliver quality experiences, effective governance and sustainable development.
On the way to building strong cultural and tourism industries, China is more confident in realizing its ambitious inbound tourism goal. In the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural and tourism development, the target is to attract 190 million inbound tourist visits a year by 2030.
To reach that goal, China will continue to make travel easier for international tourists in areas such as visa-free policy, payment, tax refund, accommodation and transportation.
Easier access and more options, from hairstyling and dental care to traditional Chinese medicine and custom tailoring, will bring longer stays by overseas visitors.
"This allows them to see a more authentic, diverse and vibrant side of China," said Hu Yang, senior vice president of Tujia. ■

Now, nine months after Yair Netanyahu was urgently evacuated from Miami, i24NEWS has reported new details about the operation.
According to a US law-enforcement source cited by Newsmax, Israeli intelligence uncovered an Iranian plot in December 2025 to target the prime minister’s 35-year-old son, who was living in Hallandale Beach near Miami.
Intelligence assessments indicated that a suspected Iranian cell was already operating in the Miami area and monitoring Netanyahu’s home and daily routine.
Col. (res.) A separate report said Netanyahu’s security detail in Miami could not adequately respond to the threat. Two additional teams assigned to President Isaac Herzog, including a senior commander, were therefore sent from New York, where they were accompanying the president on an official visit.
The reinforcements reportedly helped evacuate Netanyahu to the airport, from where he flew to Israel later that night.
Yair Netanyahu had already taken extensive precautions during his two years in Miami because of concerns for his safety. At times, he reportedly avoided stepping onto the balconies of his residence, even before the alleged plot was uncovered.
Following the disclosure, the prime minister defended the extensive protection provided to his family.

In July, the Shin Bet extended security protection for Netanyahu’s wife, Sara, and his sons, Yair and Avner. His sons are reportedly expected to remain under protection for five years after Netanyahu leaves office.
The Shin Bet later confirmed that authorities had identified a “significant threat” against Yair Netanyahu. Following a security assessment, officials decided to evacuate him and his protection team to Israel immediately.

Turkish defense firm Aselsan has demonstrated electronic warfare and radar systems on Baykar’s Bayraktar TB2 drones in Konya, with defense delegations from 18 countries attending.
One drone carried the Antidot 2ES 100 electronic support pod and Antidot 2EA 200 electronic warfare pod. A second carried the Fulmar 200 synthetic aperture radar system.
During the first test, the Antidot systems detected and located a target radar before carrying out an electronic attack, allowing the drone to approach without being detected, Aselsan said.
In the second test, Antidot located another target and shared its coordinates with Fulmar 200, which produced high-resolution radar images of the site.
The company said the demonstration combined detection, location, jamming and imaging in a single operational sequence. It marked the first test of Antidot systems against live radars aboard the TB2, according to Aselsan.
The electronic support pod identifies radar signals and relays information to ground control stations. The electronic warfare pod can autonomously counter search and tracking radars using preprogrammed techniques.
Fulmar 200 is designed to provide radar imagery by day and night in all weather conditions. It can be mounted beneath a wing or on the aircraft’s body and used alongside optical and infrared cameras.

issey miyake turns matisse cut-outs into clothing and choreography at tate modern
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:45:59 UTC
16:45:59 KST

Inside Tate Modern’s South Tank, the performance begins as guests entered the room. A pale felt surface covered the floor, with benches following the circular concrete wall and individual seats scattered closer to its center. Lying across the floor was a pleated garment shaped after one of the paper cut-outs in Henri Matisse’s The Snail (1953). Then a performer began lifting sections of felt to reveal more clothing underneath.
Presented on September 16th, 2026 as the second edition of HOMME PLISSÉ ISSEY MIYAKE’s OPEN STUDIO, the evening placed the audience directly inside the structure of the dance. Performers approached individual guests and invited them to sit for sessions of One One One, a format developed by Ioannis Mandafounis in which a dancer creates choreography live in response to the person in front of them. Eye contact holds the exchange together. Around them, the rest of the room watches these encounters take shape one by one. View the performance here!
As the sessions continued, performers pulled garments from beneath the felt and slipped them on. Shapes familiar from The Snail (1953) began moving independently across the room. In Matisse’s composition, colored paper sits flat against a white ground. Here, those same geometries stretch across shoulders and torsos, while HOMME PLISSÉ ISSEY MIYAKE’s pleats expand and contract with each movement.
The idea came from the design team’s first encounter with the work. They describe wanting to ‘animate each paper cut-out by translating it into a garment,’ using their pleating process to give Matisse’s forms another kind of movement. During the performance, dancers repeatedly changed clothes and placed the discarded pieces across the stage, recalling the loose paper forms that once filled Matisse’s studio. The source image gradually disperses across the room rather than remaining fixed at its center.
performers move through the Tate Modern’s South Tank
the stage loses its fixed front
The South Tank gives the exchange room to move in every direction. Its raw concrete perimeter surrounds a broad open floor, while the seating arrangement leaves people embedded within the performance area itself. In the wider views, dancers cross between seated guests as other performers occupy distant corners of the room. Attention keeps shifting. A person who is watching can suddenly become the person being watched.
That spatial setup suits Mandafounis’s One One One. The method asks dancers to translate sensations prompted by an audience member’s presence into movement, giving each encounter its own duration and rhythm. The spectator influences what happens simply by being there. Meanwhile, everyone sitting along the outer wall sees a series of small performances forming across the room, each with its own temporary center.
dancers retrieve pleated garments hidden beneath the felt flooring throughout the performance
from image to body and back again
Toward the end, the exchange changes again. A single performer appears on the floor before the others return and pull back the felt at the center of the Tank. Beneath it is a full-scale reconstruction of The Snail (1953) assembled from the pleated garments, with each piece cut to match the geometry of Matisse’s original composition. The dancers gather around it and continue moving as the fragmented image comes back together.
For much of the performance, Matisse’s image exists through people. Its forms bend around bodies and travel through the room. By the closing sequence, those garments return to the floor and become an image again. The audience also changes position within that cycle. Earlier, an individual spectator could prompt the choreography directly. At the end, everyone faces the same composition. OPEN STUDIO turns that shift between participation and observation into part of the work itself.
the audience sits along the circular perimeter as dancers move across the felt-covered floor
pleated garments translate the paper cut-outs of Henri Matisse’s The Snail (1953) into moving forms
One One One pairs individual spectators with performers for improvised encounters sustained through eye contact
performers change between garments as the composition disperses across the South Tank
the performance moves between direct audience encounters and a central, shared view of The Snail (1953)

Google's AI independently infiltrated three external systems, mistakenly believing they were test systems
Kyiv • UNN
Gemini mistakenly identified real systems as test systems and gained access to three of them. Google said that no harm was done.
Google's Gemini artificial intelligence model gained unauthorized access to three external computer systems during testing, using login credentials it found or guessed on its own. The AI believed the real systems were part of the test environment, NBC News reports, citing Google, writes UNN.
Details
The incidents occurred in May 2026 while Gemini's capabilities were being evaluated. In two cases, the model used credentials it found publicly available, while in the other cases it was able to guess the information required to log in.
Google Vice President of Security Engineering Heather Adkins said that Gemini was convinced the external systems were part of the testing. After gaining access, the model did not continue taking actions inside the systems.
Gemini confused the test environment with the real Internet
During a standard evaluation, the model found publicly available information on the Internet and guessed credentials to access websites that it believed were part of the test
Google does not consider these incidents to be a deliberate deviation by the AI from the instructions it was given. According to the company, the cause was an incorrect identification of the environment: Gemini believed it was continuing to operate within a controlled test, although it actually had access to the real Internet.
Google claims that the incidents caused no harm. The company learned about them in July after an additional review conducted by the cybersecurity company Irregular, which was testing Gemini.
Following the investigation, Google notified the owners of the relevant systems and the U.S. federal authorities about the unauthorized access.

MSF launches Ebola vaccination study among DRC frontline workers
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:42:46 UTC
16:42:46 KST

Bunia, Democratic Republic of Congo – As the Ebola disease outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) and Epicentre, MSF’s epidemiological research centre, are launching a vaccination study, BRAVO.1 The significant study will follow frontline workers in the Ebola response over time to assess the effect of the ERVEBO vaccine. The study is integrated into the Ministry of Health-led outbreak response. No vaccine or treatment specifically targeting Bundibugyo virus is immediately available.
Conducted with the Ministry of Health, Africa CDC, the Congolese National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB), and scientific partners, the study will document and evaluate the use of ERVEBO, the only Ebola vaccine currently available at scale. The vaccine has a well-established safety profile and has been widely used in DRC. However, it was developed and licensed for the Zaire virus of Ebola disease, not Bundibugyo virus, which is driving the current outbreak.
“Although ERVEBO was not originally developed to protect against Bundibugyo, preliminary data suggest that it may offer some degree of protection against the virus,” says Dr Guyguy Manangama, epidemiologist and deputy director of operations at MSF. “In a race against time such as the one the DRC is currently facing, we must use every tool available to us.”
Even partial protection could help reduce severe illness and deaths... That is precisely the purpose of BRAVO.
“Even partial protection could help reduce severe illness and deaths,” says Dr Manangama. “However, these potential benefits must be demonstrated scientifically. That is precisely the purpose of BRAVO.”
Launched on 19 September at the World Health Organization (WHO)-run training centre for health workers in Bunia, the study will run for a period of nine to 12 months. This will include three months dedicated to vaccination and a minimum of six months of participant follow-up. It will target 20,000 frontline workers in Ituri and North Kivu provinces, a group at particularly high risk of exposure to the virus and essential to the outbreak response. The study will generate real-world data on the use of the ERVEBO vaccine and its potential effectiveness in the current outbreak context.
Several vaccines specifically targeting Bundibugyo virus are under development and may become available in the coming months. Continuing and accelerating this research remains essential. In the meantime, ERVEBO is being offered as an interim measure because of its established safety profile and its approval by several leading regulatory authorities, including the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the European Medicines Agency, and WHO.
Participation in BRAVO and vaccination are entirely voluntary. Vaccination is an additional protective measure; it does not replace proven infection prevention and control measures. All frontline workers must continue to use protective equipment, follow safe-care procedures, and report symptoms quickly.
“It is important to stress that this vaccine will not end the current outbreak,” says Dr Manangama. “However, it may offer additional protection to those most exposed, and help strengthen the response alongside other essential interventions.”

'Deeply offensive' to suggest farmers 'prefer to abuse and exploit backpackers', NFF says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:40:34 UTC
16:40:34 KST

IN BRIEF
- Australia's peak farming body says new visa limits could leave growers short of workers during key harvest periods.
- The body has rejected any suggestion that farmers rely on backpackers because Pacific workers are harder to exploit.
Australia's peak farming body has accused Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke of making "deeply offensive" comments about farmers, as concern grows over how changes to backpacker visas could affect the nation's agricultural workforce.
The National Farmers' Federation (NFF) has warned the changes could contribute to higher food prices if they leave growers without enough workers during key harvest periods — times when farmers often hire 'backpackers' on Working Holiday visas.
While Burke acknowledged the migration changes would create challenges for some, he suggested the agricultural sector could utilise additional capacity in the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) scheme.
The scheme allows eligible Australian businesses to recruit workers from nine Pacific island countries and Timor-Leste when there are not enough local workers available.
Burke also said the strengthening of protections for PALM workers during his tenure as employment minister had led to warnings from some agricultural employers that they would turn away from the PALM scheme.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
"At the time that we were improving those rules, we had some of the farm organisations say to us, 'If you do this, our members will just go and use backpackers,'" Burke told SBS News.
"If the reason that people are more reliant on backpackers and refusing to use Pacific workers is because they're upset that we've ended exploitation in those areas, I think that is a very different question for a number of operators."
He also stressed the criticism did not apply to the entire agricultural sector, saying "that doesn't depict the whole of the farm sector, not for a minute".
Richard Shannon, executive officer of the NFF Horticulture Council, labelled Burke's comments as "provocative" and rejected any suggestion that employers had moved away from the PALM scheme because of stronger protections for workers.
"The minister is suggesting that employers in horticulture would prefer to abuse and exploit backpackers than remain in the PALM program," Shannon told SBS News.
"This is not about exploiting people and finding loopholes, and it's deeply offensive."
Shannon argued that the reason some employers had moved away from PALM was because changes to the scheme had increased costs and administrative requirements.
He said backpackers and PALM workers also served different purposes within the agricultural workforce and could not simply be substituted for one another.
Employers in the PALM scheme have responsibilities including arranging accommodation and transport and providing additional support to workers.
Shannon said those requirements made the scheme significantly more expensive for employers than hiring backpackers, particularly for businesses needing workers for shorter periods.
The changes come as parts of Australia's horticulture industry approach major summer harvest periods, when growers can require large numbers of workers for relatively short periods.
"What [Burke] is effectively doing now is shortening the supply of backpackers and pushing people, employers, back into a program that is uncommercial for them," he said.
Why are farmers concerned about the visa changes?
Under the federal government's migration overhaul announced on Thursday, working holidaymakers wanting to remain in Australia for a second or third year will have to enter a ballot after completing the required regional work.
Second-year places will be capped at 45,000, compared with 57,000 people who qualified last year, while third-year places will fall from 31,000 to 5,000.
The government says the changes will give it greater control over migration numbers while retaining incentives for backpackers to work in regional Australia.
The government has also announced agriculture will receive priority under changes to skilled visa processing.
Shannon said the agricultural sector's immediate reaction to the changes has been "alarm", and farmers were seeking more detail from the government about how the changes would affect workforce availability.
"We have no detail as to what effect this might have on the workforce that's available in the short term and ongoing," he said.
"That's so important for our growers right now — to better understand what effect this is going to have on the numbers of backpackers in the region, and whether or not they need to make alternative plans."
Shannon also said any significant shortage of workers could ultimately flow through to consumers through higher production costs.
"It's quite clear that there's going to be a shortage now of workers, and that prices of food are going to go up."
Shannon said agricultural worker shortages during the COVID-19 pandemic had also led to such price rises but added that the industry was still uncertain about exactly how Labor's changes would affect worker availability during key harvest periods.
The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics and Sciences reported in late 2021 that fruit and vegetable prices had risen above their usual seasonal levels but said declining availability of overseas agricultural workers was only one possible cause.
What's happening to Working Holiday visas?
The government's recently announced changes form part of a broader effort to bring net overseas migration down to 245,000 this financial year and 225,000 in 2027-28.
Burke said working holidaymakers accounted for 48,000 places in the nation's net overseas migration figure last year, arguing no part of the visa system could be excluded from efforts to reduce overall numbers.
Backpackers will still need to complete 88 days of specified regional work to qualify for a second year and six months to qualify for a third.
But completing that work will no longer guarantee an additional year. Eligible applicants will instead enter the new ballots for the limited number of places.
At the same time, the government says processing of primary working holidaymaker applications will return to faster rates for countries whose visa arrangements include the regional work requirement.
Shannon said the NFF wanted the government to leave the existing working holidaymaker arrangements in place rather than impose the new caps.

- North Korean state media said Kim Jong Un toured munitions factories from Sept. 16 to 18, inspecting production tied to a rocket launcher resembling the U.S. HIMARS system.
- The visit follows a May 2026 test of the launcher alongside an upgraded 240mm rocket and an AI-guided cruise missile Kim ordered deployed near the South Korean border.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un toured major munitions factories over three days, from Sept. 16 to 18, inspecting weapons production that reportedly included a mobile rocket launcher Western analysts have compared to the U.S. Army’s HIMARS system, state media reported Sept. 19.
The ruling Workers’ Party newspaper Rodong Sinmun said Kim, the party’s general secretary, visited “important munitions industry enterprises” to check on production conditions. Kim told factory officials the military must “constantly load the most powerful and overwhelming strategic force” into the armed forces, according to the report, and pressed the plants to expand output.
The visit follows a pattern Kim has repeated for years, touring weapons factories every few months and calling for faster, larger-scale production. He made similar visits in August 2023, January 2024 and December 2025, each time emphasizing what state media described as the “paramount importance” of missile and artillery output to the country’s war readiness.
The launcher system tied to this week’s visit first appeared publicly at a 2023 military parade and was tested for the first time on May 26, 2026, alongside two other weapons: an upgraded 240mm guided rocket and a tactical cruise missile North Korea says uses artificial intelligence for terminal guidance.
Photos released by North Korean state media at the time showed a wheeled vehicle carrying a small number of launch tubes, a configuration that resembles the U.S. Army’s M142 HIMARS, a truck-mounted system that fires precision-guided rockets from a single launcher and has seen extensive combat use in Ukraine. South Korea’s military detected the May test independently, tracking projectiles that flew roughly 80 km (50 miles) toward the Yellow Sea, though Seoul did not confirm North Korea’s specific claims about the systems involved.
Kim ordered the accelerated deployment of the AI-guided cruise missile to front-line artillery units near the South Korean border after that May test, calling the results “a clear signal” of North Korea’s military progress. This week’s factory tour suggests the program has moved from testing toward production, though North Korea did not disclose how many units of any system have been built or where the factories are located, following its usual practice of withholding exact locations from state media coverage.
The factory visit came the same week North Korea rejected a resolution the International Atomic Energy Agency adopted criticizing its nuclear weapons program. North Korean officials said the country’s status as a nuclear power is permanently written into domestic law and does not require international recognition, a position Pyongyang has maintained consistently in response to IAEA and U.N. criticism.

Macron heading to Saint Pierre and Miquelon to meet with Canadian PM Carney
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:38:46 UTC
16:38:46 KST

French President Emmanuel Macron is travelling to Saint Pierre and Miquelon this weekend, an archipelago the Élysée describes as "central to today's France."
French President Emmanuel Macron is travelling to Saint Pierre and Miquelon this weekend to discuss the future of the archipelago, as well as France's geostrategic presence in the North Atlantic, maritime sovereignty and cooperation with Ottawa.
The last French president to make a trip to the overseas collectivity, which is located some 20 kilometres off the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador, was François Hollande back in December 2014.
Eleven years on, Macron will be there on Sunday alongside Mark Carney, the Canadian prime minister.
Their meeting comes amid Carney's apparently blossoming relationship with Brussels and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's proposal to make Canada an associate member of the EU.
An archipelago 'central to today's France'
The key goal of the trip is to "deliver a message (...) about France's presence across five oceans," the French presidency said during a telephone briefing with the media, including Euronews. France has a presence in the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans, as well as "in the Arctic, through Saint Pierre and Miquelon" and in the Southern Ocean.
Located at the gateway to the Arctic, Saint Pierre and Miquelon gives France a significant exclusive economic zone and allows it to maintain a military presence there.
That presence is partly provided by the Fulmar, a navy patrol vessel and the only French military ship permanently based in the archipelago, which is due for replacement.
Saint Pierre and Miquelon is not a peripheral outpost, the Élysée stresses, but "a territory, an archipelago that is central to today's France."
During the presidential visit, questions of sovereignty will also be discussed in relation to digital cables and connections linking the archipelago and the European continent, as well as space-related activities, where further investment expected.
Another item on the agenda will be regional cooperation. Paris wants to turn Saint Pierre and Miquelon into a "rear base for polar cooperation," working not only with Canada but also with Denmark and Greenland.
The president is also expected to focus on the day-to-day difficulties faced by residents.
Saint Pierre and Miquelon is grappling with economic and social problems similar to those seen in many isolated territories around the world while also experiencing the effects of climate change.
The archipelago's population is also declining. The biggest blow came with the collapse of the fishing industry following years of a Canadian moratorium on cod fishing. France also saw its exclusive economic zone there reduced following a court ruling in 1992.
Another threat facing the territory is rising sea levels. The village of Miquelon-Langlade, located on a narrow strip of sand just two metres above sea level, is being moved farther inland. It is the first relocation project carried out in France in response to the effects of global warming.
Canada, a new energy partner?
Paris supports closer ties between Brussels and Ottawa and has reiterated its willingness to work with all countries that "share our values and want to strengthen their ability to decide, produce and act for themselves."
The practical details of this new partnership, however, have yet to be worked out.
Energy could become one of its main areas of focus.
France is looking to Canada to help secure European supplies of hydrocarbons, at a time when fuel prices are soaring due to global conflicts and tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.
This situation is already putting additional pressure on France's heavily indebted public finances, forcing the government to extend some existing measures and step up talks with partners, particularly in the Middle East.
Macron and Carney are due to continue their talks next week in New York, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

First new wild cat discovered in a century
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:36:33 UTC
16:36:33 KST

The newly identified Tilcayo cat walks through the Yungas forest.
Scientists have discovered a new species of wild cat for the first time in more than a century, a Bolivian researcher said on Sept. 17.
The Tilcayo tiger cat, a small feline with a spotted, leopard-like coat, was identified in the mountainous Yungas region near the capital La Paz.
Locals who saw the creature in the Bolivian Andes had mistaken it for an ordinary house cat, said biologist and National Geographic explorer Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, who was part of the research team that studied them.
The nickname “tilcayo” given to the animal by locals inspired its new scientific designation: Leopardus tilcayo.
Nogales-Ascarrunz lauded the discovery as a “remarkable event, because a new wild cat species hasn’t been described in 100 years.” The cat is the first new feline discovered since the Uruguayan pampas cat in 1923.
The tilcayo is slightly smaller than a domestic cat, measuring around 45 centimeters, with rounded ears. A pair of tilcayos, the only such creatures found so far, have undergone whole genome sequencing, Nogales-Ascarrunz said, referring to a type of in-depth genetic testing.
A male tilcayo is living at an animal shelter in Yungas, after it was handed over by a family who had taken in the creature.
A female was rescued and released into the wild after being attacked by locals.
Research on the species was published on Sept. 17 in the journal Current Biology, capping off research that scientists began in 2021.
“So far, it’s only been detected in Bolivia” and not “anywhere else on the planet,” Nogales-Ascarrunz said. She said the creatures were classified as vulnerable to extinction.

Sichuan is not just about spice
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:36:22 UTC
16:36:22 KST

If you think Sichuan cuisine is all about spicy food, then you haven’t really discovered it yet. On my first visit, I too expected a cuisine dominated by chillies, Sichuan pepper and hotpot. Yet what stayed with me was not the intensity of the spice, but the extraordinary complexity and layering of flavours. A single mouthful can begin with chilli heat, followed by that distinctive numbing tingle, then sweetness, acidity, fermentation and umami. Sometimes it is difficult to find two dishes on the same table that taste remotely alike.
That complexity is precisely what has earned Sichuan its place among China’s most important regional cuisines. Its capital, Chengdu, has been part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network as a City of Gastronomy since 2010, and UNESCO highlights the cuisine’s remarkable ability to balance sweet, sour, bitter, spicy and salty flavours. There is even a saying in China that captures Chengdu’s culinary reputation rather neatly: “Food is in China, but flavour is in Chengdu.”
The flavour sensation most closely associated with Sichuan cooking around the world is málà. The word describes two distinct sensations working together. Là is the heat of chilli; má is the peculiar tingling, numbing effect of Sichuan pepper, a sensation that can feel almost electric on the tongue. Bring the two together and the result is not simply greater spiciness. Combined with oils, aromatics, spices and fermented ingredients, they create a succession of sensations and flavours that seems to evolve as you eat.
Perhaps the greatest misconception about Sichuan cuisine is that it begins and ends with málà. Traditional Sichuan cooking encompasses dozens of distinct flavour profiles. Sweet-and-sour, garlicky, sesame-rich, pickled, fermented and red-oil preparations sit alongside dishes that can be surprisingly subtle and delicate. Sichuan cooking techniques have been recognised as part of China’s national intangible cultural heritage, while UNESCO’s report on Chengdu refers to 24 distinct flavour profiles within the cuisine.
Nor does Sichuan have a single culinary identity. Chengdu is the centre of a particularly refined and intricately layered style of Sichuan cooking. Nearby Leshan is a food destination in its own right, famous for street food and small bites, from tofu pudding and skewers to dumplings and shaomai. Travel further south and you reach Zigong, whose distinctive food culture grew out of the wealth generated by its historic salt industry. It is the heartland of yanbangcai, often translated as “salt merchants’ cuisine,” an important tradition within the broader Sichuan repertoire. Yibin, meanwhile, has its own distinctive noodle dishes and a taste for bold, assertive flavours. Saying “I’ve eaten Sichuan food” is therefore a little like saying “I’ve eaten Mediterranean food”: Travel a few hundred kilometres and the ingredients, the intensity of the spice and even the way people eat can change considerably.
Chengdu’s restaurant scene is also going through an interesting transformation. The 2027 Michelin Guide Chengdu, announced on 11 September, offers a revealing snapshot of how far the city has come. The selection includes 84 restaurants: One with three Michelin stars, one with two and 13 with one star. For the first time, Chengdu has a three-Michelin-starred restaurant. More significantly, the guide points to a new generation of chefs reinterpreting traditional techniques through contemporary ideas, with local produce and cultural identity playing an increasingly prominent role in their cooking.
For me, this is where Chengdu becomes particularly exciting. Tiny noodle shops where a bowl still costs only a few yuan, wonton specialists and traditional teahouses continue to thrive, while alongside them a serious contemporary dining scene is emerging, with chefs finding new ways to express Sichuan’s culinary heritage.
Perhaps what makes Sichuan so compelling today is precisely the fact that these two worlds can coexist. On one side are centuries of knowledge about fermentation, traditional teahouses, markets, bubbling hotpots and recipes passed down through families; on the other, a younger generation of chefs beginning to translate that inheritance into a contemporary culinary language.
HH ENTERING CHINA THROUGH A DIFFERENT GATEWAY
On this trip to China, I flew with Sichuan Airlines. It was my first time travelling with the carrier, and when I looked into the airline and saw the figures, I was surprised by its scale. Sichuan Airlines today operates an all-Airbus fleet of more than 200 aircraft and carries over 35 million passengers a year. According to the latest figures provided by the airline, its fleet has reached 213 aircraft and its network now covers 151 destinations.
Its story, in some ways, mirrors China’s extraordinary growth over the past four decades. Founded in 1986, Sichuan Airlines operated its first flight between Chengdu and Wanzhou in 1988. When the company was restructured in 2002, its fleet consisted of just 12 aircraft. Today, it is the fifth Chinese airline to have passed the 200-aircraft mark. It was also the first airline in mainland China to operate the Airbus A320 — an interesting detail in the story of a carrier that has since built an entirely Airbus fleet.
I flew business class from Istanbul to Chengdu. And in fact, you don’t have to wait until you land to get your first taste of Sichuan; the character of the region begins to reveal itself on board. The cabin crew’s charming panda aprons during meal service are the first playful detail. More importantly for me, however, was the food. Regional flavours appear on the menu, so your introduction to Sichuan cuisine can begin at 10,000 metres. On long-haul flights, where airlines often gravitate towards dishes designed to appeal to the broadest possible range of palates, I liked the fact that Sichuan Airlines allowed the destination to make its presence felt before we had even arrived.
Once you land in Chengdu, a very different side of China opens up. From its home base, the airline flies to major cities including Lhasa, Kunming, Sanya, Hangzhou and Nanjing, as well as destinations such as Xishuangbanna, Dali and Daocheng, which are considerably less straightforward to reach from Türkiye. For me, that is one of the most interesting aspects of flying into Chengdu: It offers an alternative gateway to western and southwestern China. The airline’s international network was broader than I had expected, too. Sichuan Airlines has branded its international expansion “Panda Routes,” and its network today extends across Asia, Europe, Africa, Oceania and North America.
Its ownership structure is another interesting detail. Sichuan Airlines is independently managed, yet its shareholders include all three of China’s major state-owned airline groups. Sichuan Airlines Group holds the largest stake at 40 per cent, followed by China Southern at 39 per cent, while China Eastern and Air China each hold 10 per cent. The remaining one per cent belongs to Chengdu Gingko Restaurant Co. — a small detail that, as a food writer, naturally caught my attention.
But beyond the fleet sizes, passenger numbers and route maps, what interests me most is where an airline can take you. A good air connection does more than shorten the distance between two cities; sometimes it opens up a journey you might never otherwise have thought of making.
Sichuan is a perfect example. You can spend several days in Chengdu eating your way from hotpot and dan dan mian to mapo tofu, while discovering the city’s wonderful teahouse culture, and then continue your journey into an entirely different part of China. Sichuan Airlines’ extensive domestic network also means there is no reason to experience the country solely along the familiar Beijing–Shanghai axis. Even within Sichuan itself, Chengdu makes an excellent starting point for a food journey through Leshan, Zigong and Yibin.
Perhaps the most interesting thought I brought home from this journey was this: In a country as vast as China, the gateway through which you enter can shape the China you ultimately discover. This time, that gateway was Chengdu. And I didn’t even have to wait until landing to begin discovering Sichuan; from the panda aprons to the regional flavours, the journey had already begun on board.
For someone like me, who so often plans a journey around what I am going to eat when I get there, it is difficult to imagine a more delicious beginning.

Wildfire risk persists in Türkiye despite autumn rain
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:35:32 UTC
16:35:32 KST

(AA Photo)
Favorable rain created ideal ignition environments by boosting plant growth, experts said, urging authorities to maintain strict preventive measures as autumn arrives.
The situation does not mean the fire season has ended, Isparta Applied Sciences University Rector Yılmaz Çatal said in the southern province of Isparta. High temperatures, low humidity and strong winds alter fire behavior within hours, making Türkiye’s outlook fragile amid Western European heat waves.
August and September form the critical period, as high temperatures in southern and western Anatolia prepare vegetation for ignition. Human activity causes nearly 90 percent of fires, Çatal said. Northern rainfall triggers dry northeasterly winds in the south, complicating firefighting while summer conditions continue in the Aegean and Mediterranean.
Officials must supervise agricultural activities, industrial facilities, energy lines and forest-rural interfaces. Çatal said assigning duties to neighborhood heads and police is essential during this period.
Türkiye recorded a milder 2026 season due to weather and firefighting capacity, but officials must use dynamic risk maps combining meteorological data, terrain, past fires and human mobility. Expanding artificial intelligence, cameras, satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles will help manage these risks, Çatal said, pointing to climate predictions showing the Mediterranean basin will warm faster than the global average.
Heavy rains increased combustible material loads nationwide, Karadeniz Technical University Forestry Faculty Professor Ertuğrul Bilgili said in the northern province of Trabzon. “This increase in combustible material paves the way for a fire to start, grow and develop into a hazard,” he said.
Bilgili said uncontrollable fires strike when combustible moisture drops below 10 percent during strong winds, making mid-July to early August the peak danger period for the Aegean and Mediterranean.
Negligence causes over half of the fires, making public training on evacuation, stubble burning, garden waste clearance and picnic fires essential alongside socio-economic expectations. Officials must base fire prevention on scientific foundations and special funds, expanding controlled burning and using helicopters as primary aerial vehicles, Bilgili said.
Türkiye’s climate causes long, dry summers, leaving coasts highly susceptible to rapid fire spread. The country completely overhauled its emergency response strategies following the 2021 wildfires.

Protesters form human chain at Kennedy Center in US after Trump threat
Unknown

Protesters form human chain at Kennedy Center in US after Trump threat
WASHINGTON - Protesters formed a human chain on Sept 18 around the Kennedy Center, the Washington arts hub that US President Donald Trump threatened to demolish unless his name is restored to it.
The complex’s main building has been shuttered since Sept 16 – temporarily, according to its leadership – while a judge is also reviewing plans for a long-term closure to accommodate Trump’s desired renovations of the ageing facility.
Crowds waved placards reading “hands off Kennedy Center” and broke out into song beneath the scaffolding and tarps that have remained in place since workers removed Trump’s name from the building in June following a court order.
Trump took control in 2025 of the Kennedy Center – inaugurated in 1971 following the assassination of US president John F Kennedy – and has pushed for a major renovation, claiming the building had been left in a state of disrepair by previous leaders.
Like other projects around the US capital, the president has shown an unprecedented keenness to put his personal touch on plans, while testing the legal bounds of executive authority.
Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board voted in 2025 to officially rename the institution as the Trump-Kennedy Center, with corresponding updates to building signage and online logos.
The move – later reversed by a judge – led to a major decline in ticket sales, artist boycotts and an exodus of donors, according to The Washington Post.
‘Not a political place’
“It makes me sick to my stomach,” said Neal Racioppo, a Washington resident who runs marketing and communications for a theatre.
Trump “can’t get his name on this cherished building, so he is depriving the world of what it could be.”
Racioppo, 57, joined a human chain that formed as night fell on the imposing, white, marble building, with crowds sprawling out onto the esplanade overlooking the Potomac River.
Demonstrators were zigzagged around the barriers installed after the centre closed this week, with some waving placards reading “hands off Kennedy Center” and “Donny, you are no JFK”.
“It has been an important home for the arts for this city and this country and the world,” Racioppo said.
“What President Trump is doing is despicable.”
Lizzy Andrew, who has performed several times at the Kennedy Center, including singing with the National Symphony Orchestra, said she was angered at Trump’s threat to tear down the venue.
“He does not have a right to decide that an institution, a living memorial to a past president, can be demolished,” the 30-year-old told AFP.
“I think you can see tonight that the people of DC and the people of America do not agree with that decision.”
Lela Agnew, who regularly brings her children to visit the centre, said she came to defend an institution that “belongs to the people”.

Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe and is ready to restore relations and cooperate with its European neighbors, said President Vladimir Putin.
Speaking at a meeting of the Military-Industrial Commission on Friday, Putin accused some European leaders of preparing for war with Russia and said they were using the conflict in Ukraine and the alleged Russian threat to justify their policies.
“I want to state once again: Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe or European countries,” he said. “There are simply no grounds for this whatsoever. We are ready for cooperation and for restoring relations with our European neighbors.”
He criticized European countries for holding military exercises in the Baltic Sea, saying they included preparations to seize civilian vessels.
“They constantly talk about defending international law and upholding its norms, yet they prepare to seize civilian vessels,” Putin said.
He said Moscow would respond if necessary. “Let us live in peace -- otherwise, we, too, will be forced to respond.”

“And this thoroughly corrupt regime -- is it really the main defender of democracy in Europe? That sounds a bit odd,” he said.

Putin also outlined priorities for Russia’s new State Armament Program, saying it would focus on modernizing the armed forces and defense industry amid what he described as evolving global threats.
He identified strengthening Russia’s nuclear triad as the program’s “absolute priority,” saying it guarantees sovereignty and helps maintain the global balance of power.
Putin said 92% of Russia’s Strategic Missile Forces are equipped with modern weapons.
He listed strengthening air defense, expanding unmanned and robotic systems, developing precision-strike weapons and completing Russia’s orbital satellite constellation among key priorities.
The satellite network, he said, would improve space-based reconnaissance, navigation, communications and broadband internet capabilities while enabling real-time command and control of troops and weapons.

U.S. approves Ukraine air defense package with unclear weapons
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:27:59 UTC
16:27:59 KST

- The U.S. State Department approved a possible $2.68 billion air defense sale to Ukraine on Sept. 18, funded through European contributions and prior U.S. military financing.
- The package lists "S-300 Clone" and "GAM-67" missiles, designations that don't match any publicly known current weapon system.
The U.S. State Department approved a possible $2.68 billion sale of air defense equipment to Ukraine on Sept. 18, a package built around several weapons whose exact identity the notification itself does not make clear.
The Defense Security Cooperation Agency’s notification to Congress describes the deal as an “Air Defense Development Upgrade.” Ukraine would pay for it through a mix of European contributions and U.S. Foreign Military Financing that Congress appropriated under the prior administration, with that American funding counted as a one-to-one capital contribution to the Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. The sale still needs to clear the standard congressional review period before any contract can be finalized, and the eventual contractors would be chosen through a competitive U.S. government procurement process.
The equipment list includes items called S-300 Clone missiles and GAM-67 missiles, along with Range-Extended Air Defense Laser Guided Rocket missile systems, a launcher platform called the Improvised Transporter Erector Launcher 1.5, mobile launcher modification kits, and RPS 202 counter-drone radars, plus the usual mix of spare parts, software, training publications and logistics support that accompanies most Foreign Military Sales packages.
Two of those names don’t match any publicly known current weapon system. GAM-67 is the U.S. Air Force’s old designation for the Crossbow, a turbojet-powered anti-radar missile program that Northrop’s Ventura Division built in the 1950s. Only 14 were ever produced, and the Air Force canceled the program in 1957 because the missile was too slow to be useful against modern air defenses. That history makes it clear the notification isn’t describing a Cold War-era leftover; the designation appears to have been reused, whether as a placeholder or a formal label for something new, rather than referring to the original Crossbow. “S-300 Clone” is similarly undefined in any public Pentagon or industry documentation, and no other name for it has surfaced.
The most plausible explanation available comes from outside the official notification. Robert Hamilton, a retired U.S. Army colonel who now leads the Delphi Global Research Center, told PBS NewsHour that the United States and Ukraine have been working jointly either to modernize Ukraine’s aging stock of S-300 interceptor missiles or to develop a newer version of the missile with improved capability. Hamilton said he expects that upgraded system to become operational close to the end of 2026. Neither the State Department nor Ukraine’s government has confirmed that this effort is the same program referenced as “S-300 Clone” in Friday’s notification, but the timing and subject matter line up closely enough that the two appear connected.
The S-300 is a Soviet-designed, long-range surface-to-air missile system that Ukraine inherited in large numbers and has relied on throughout the war, alongside Western systems like the Patriot. Ukraine has faced a persistent shortage of S-300 interceptors because Russia is now the only producer of the original missile, making any American-backed alternative, cloned, modernized or newly built, a potentially significant addition to Ukraine’s ability to keep those launchers firing.
The State Department’s notification includes the standard language used in nearly all such filings: the sale would not require additional U.S. government or contractor personnel in Ukraine, would not affect U.S. military readiness, and would not alter the basic military balance in the region. No offset agreement has been proposed so far; any such arrangement would be negotiated separately between Ukraine and whichever companies win the eventual contracts.
What remains unclear is what the S-300 Clone and GAM-67 items actually are, technically or physically. Congress has not yet completed its review, and neither Washington nor Kyiv has released further detail on the specifications, quantities, or delivery timeline for either item.

The James Webb Telescope has discovered mysterious worlds that astronomers had never encountered before
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
10:27:31 EEST
16:27:31 KST

The James Webb Telescope has discovered mysterious worlds that astronomers had never encountered before
Kyiv • UNN
The telescope detected brown dwarfs in IC 348 with masses of about two Jupiters. A disk was observed around one of them, where planets may be forming.
The James Webb Space Telescope has detected the least massive brown dwarfs known to date—some of them have a mass only about twice that of Jupiter. The discovery was made while studying the star-forming region IC 348, located approximately 1,000 light-years from Earth, the European Space Agency (ESA) reports, writes UNN.
Details
IC 348 is located in the constellation Perseus and is one of the closest regions of active star formation to Earth. Astronomers used Webb's capabilities to determine how small objects formed during the star-formation process can be.
Brown dwarfs form as a result of the collapse of gas clouds, just like ordinary stars. However, their mass is insufficient for hydrogen to be stably converted into helium in their cores.
The discovery surprised astronomers
In 2022, Webb had already found brown dwarfs in IC 348 with masses of approximately 3–4 Jupiters. New, deeper observations made it possible to detect objects with masses of only about 2 Jupiters, or approximately 0.19% of the Sun's mass.
According to ESA, these are the least massive brown dwarfs known. Their existence raises new questions for modern models of star formation, since objects this light were nevertheless able to form through a "stellar" process.
Astronomers discovered another surprise near one of the new brown dwarfs. It has signs of a disk of material around it, in which planets could potentially form, even though the mass of the brown dwarf itself is comparable to the masses of planets.
Researchers also detected unusual signs of hydrocarbons in the atmospheres of the smallest brown dwarfs. Scientists suggest that such extremely low-mass objects may even belong to a separate spectral class.
Along with the study's findings, ESA released a large-scale image of IC 348 taken by the telescope's NIRCam camera. It shows young stars, brown dwarfs, protostars, and jets of material expelled by newborn stars into the surrounding gas and dust.

Rail Baltica deadline shift could help Estonia tap more EU funds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:27:00 UTC
16:27:00 KST

Rail Baltica deadline shift could help Estonia tap more EU funds
Construction on the Tallinn–Pärnu section will continue, but work on other segments can be postponed, says infrastructure minister Kuldar Leis.
Intense work is underway along the Rail Baltica route in Estonia. Builders have so far operated under the assumption that trains must be running by 2030.
The government's message on Thursday — that the railway's completion deadline may be pushed back by four years — saddened construction company TREV-2's CEO Sven Pertens.
"From a builder's perspective, it's very unfortunate," said Pertens. "Construction companies have built up their resources assuming the market would remain more or less stable. If there's no work, we simply cannot keep people on payroll waiting for the possibility that maybe years later something will come up."
About ten kilometers away, another builder Verston has carved the rail corridor through more than ten meters of limestone and is preparing to cross a bog. On such difficult terrain, extra time could allow for more cost‑effective solutions, said Verston Group CEO Veiko Veskimäe.
Tallinn-Pärnu section is the most mature
"I just visited the project office and asked the site manager what the biggest problem is right now. Naturally, he said they're short on trucks," Veskimäe noted.
Rail Baltic Estonia believes that extending deadlines could cool the construction market and allow the project to rely more on EU funding.
"A longer construction period would certainly ease the situation, making it possible to build kilometers at a more reasonable price," said Rail Baltic Estonia board member Lauri Ulm.
A delay would also affect train procurement. After the failure of its first tender, Elron is preparing a new one. Elron CEO Lauri Betlem wants new trains to begin operating within Estonia by 2030.
"I think we should stick to the proposed deadline, mainly because the project becomes more expensive with each passing year," Betlem said.
Although Latvia's construction pace gives little hope that trains could run beyond Ikla by 2030, the Tallinn–Pärnu section could be completed by the end of the decade.
"The Tallinn–Pärnu section is the most mature. Construction is underway across nearly the entire stretch," Ulm said.
Minister: We must decide what's sensible
Estonia's infrastructure minister Kuldar Leis said that revising the plan requires approval from Brussels.
"On Sunday and Monday, the three Baltic transport ministers will meet in Ireland at the gathering of European transport ministers. We'll discuss this again to ensure all three Baltic states act in the same way," Leis said.
"We must look at the entire process as one whole and bring all components together. First, whether Estonia is capable of finishing by 2030. Second, our southern neighbor Latvia has not given a clear signal about their ability to continue building. Third, the EU funding period is 2028–2034. If we truly finished by 2030, a large portion of EU support would go unused. Putting all this together, it makes sense to slow the pace now," Leis explained.
The minister said the plan remains to finish the domestic section — Tallinn to Pärnu — earlier. "The regional train tender will be relaunched immediately. We are not slowing down work on the entire route. Since construction on the Tallinn–Pärnu stretch is progressing very rapidly — over 100 kilometers where work is actively underway — that will continue. But south of Pärnu, and also from Ülemiste terminal toward the port in Tallinn, we can delay the start of work."
Leis added that early next week the Baltic prime ministers will also meet to discuss Rail Baltic's new timeline. "Much depends on Latvia — whether they will specify a year or not. Once the three Baltic states agree on our shared capability, we will negotiate with the European Commission on the pace of Rail Baltica. The European view is: agree among yourselves, say what you can deliver, and complete Rail Baltica."

The Commission also began talks with Ukraine last week on joining the initiative.
South Korea would be the first Asian country to join the constellation. The business case for low-Earth orbit telecommunications constellations depends on reaching customers across multiple markets globally. Gallery: More than 50 Estonian artists take stock of what matters now

Gallery: More than 50 Estonian artists take stock of what matters now
What matters to Estonian artists right now? A major new exhibition at Tallinn's Haus Gallery offers 51 perspectives through nearly 60 never-before-displayed works.
"From the Artist's Perspective" opened Thursday, marking a new curatorial project that Haus Gallery hopes to turn into an annual tradition: a dialogue between artists and the public around issues they see as important right now.
The exhibition was assembled through an open call that drew dozens of professional artists from across generations.
With few restrictions on medium or format, artists were invited to submit one to three recent works that represented something personally meaningful to them, reflecting a significant personal position or worldview.
None of the works had been previously exhibited, and artists were asked to personally provide a few lines contextualizing each work and its significance in terms of the show. These accompanying texts, the gallery said, form an important part of the project and are included on site as well as on their website.
Nearly 60 works were ultimately selected, bringing together different artistic perspectives as well as their common threads to provide a unique collective portrait of the present moment.
Rather than imposing a single interpretation, the exhibition leaves viewers to consider what Estonian artists are depicting, what moves them and why.
51 Estonian artists
Haus Gallery, which has been active on Estonia's art scene since 1997, says the project is rooted in its conviction that art can map our emotional history and reflect what takes place in society through the personal but broadly resonant perspectives of individual artists.
Curated by Piia Ausman, the exhibition features 51 artists, including Vano Allsalu, Jaan Elken, Mall Nukke, Marko Mäetamm, Maarit Murka, Liisa Jugapuu, Mari Früling, Tiit Pääsuke, Laurentsius, Katariin Mudist, Liisa Mudist, Mari Roosvalt, Külli Suitso, Lisa Add and Valeri Vinogradov.
"From the Artist's Perspective" will remain on view through October 24.

West Nile virus is spreading across Europe; more than 650 cases have been recorded in Italy
Kyiv • UNN
More than 650 cases of West Nile virus have been registered in Italy—about half of the European total. Warming temperatures are lengthening the transmission season.
More than 650 cases of West Nile virus infection were registered in Italy in 2026 — approximately half of all recorded cases in Europe. Experts link the expansion of the infection’s range and the longer transmission season to rising temperatures, Associated Press reports, according to UNN.
Details
According to Italian health authorities, the virus is increasingly being detected in areas of the country where infections had previously been rare. West Nile virus has been considered endemic in Italy since 2020.
About 80% of those infected have no symptoms at all. In most of the remaining cases, the disease is mild, with flu-like symptoms; however, a small proportion of patients may develop severe neurological complications. Older people and patients with underlying conditions face the greatest risk.
The infection season may last until November
Antonino Bella, a researcher at Italy’s National Institute of Health, explained that higher temperatures create more favorable conditions for the reproduction of mosquitoes that transmit the virus.
Higher temperatures associated with climate change help mosquitoes reproduce and extend the transmission season, increasing the likelihood that infected mosquitoes will spread the virus among people
According to him, because of warmer weather, the virus transmission season may last as late as November in some years.

Who deserves a transplant? AI's answer isn't the same as a human doctor's
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
07:16:34 UTC
16:16:34 KST

AI chatbots make faster, more confident, but less nuanced decisions than human doctors when choosing who gets a life-saving kidney transplant.
Would you get a transplant if AI were the one deciding? New study points to differences in decision-making and prioritising between artificial intelligence language models and human doctors.
AI models show overconfidence, value different factors and oversimplify complex decisions when deciding which patient should receive a transplant, according to a new study.
For their study, researchers from Penn State University in the United States gave Large Language Models (LLMs) hypothetical scenarios, based on existing datasets from published human research on kidney allocation, where real participants had already made these same choices.
Each scenario involved two patients, Patient A and Patient B, both eligible for a single available kidney and characterised by age, health, and drinking habits. A decision maker must then choose which of the two patients should receive it.
“We ran these comparisons in a few different ways,” Hosseini said. “Sometimes we isolated just one trait at a time, sometimes we mixed several traits together to see how AI weighed competing factors, and sometimes we added a flip-a-coin option to measure indecision, a key factor present in human moral judgment.”
While human respondents tended to place greater importance on age — favouring younger over older patients — many models favoured lower alcohol consumption instead. Human decisions considered multiple factors and were more context-sensitive than those of LLMs, which often focused on a single attribute.
“First, AI chatbots often diverge from human values in how they weigh a patient’s traits,” said Hadi Hosseini, lead of the study at Penn State University. “They fixate on a single factor, like drinking habits, rather than balancing multiple considerations the way people do.”
The researchers also saw that AI did not struggle with indecision. While humans recognised there is no single objectively correct answer and decisions can rely on nuanced human moral judgements, the systems committed to a single option with little hesitation.
"When we allocate something scarce, whether it’s a kidney, a job or access to some other resource, there isn’t always a single objectively correct answer,” said John Dickerson, chief executive officer at Mozilla.ai, who collaborated in the study.
“Humans recognize that ambiguity and codify it via open debate into the allocative process. AI models often don’t.”
AI and ethical decisions
Recent interactions with AI systems increasingly require them to go beyond factual information and make value judgments, the authors noted.
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into healthcare, supporting clinical workflows, diagnosis, treatment planning and timely utilisation of scarce medical resources.
One of their applications involves decisions on allocating deceased-donor or living-donor kidneys to patients, which, according to the authors, depend on complex ethical and moral considerations.
In such high-stakes scenarios, the researchers pointed out that decisions demand not only accuracy but also alignment with human values and moral judgement.
According to the researchers, asking if AI can make moral decisions or whether they’re aligned with human values lies at the core of today’s wider debate on artificial intelligence.
“The ethical stakes are high, and AI’s role in such life-altering decisions requires deep reflection,” said Hosseini. “Moral decisions in settings like organ allocation directly determine who lives and who dies, so getting AI's role in them right isn't optional.”
“While we do not intend to encourage the use of AI as a substitute for professional judgment in medical decision-making or other high-stakes contexts, it's becoming essential to understand their behavior as individuals, organizations and firms more and more rely on AI to make decisions or receive recommendations,” he added

07:16:22 UTC
16:16:22 KST

The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan rose to at least 31, including 16 police personnel, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday, with fighting ongoing.
Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex at Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, on Friday afternoon.
The police compound serves as a district-level police headquarters, housing key offices of the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), Special Branch and several other police units.
"At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and more than 100 injured so far in the militant attack and suicide bombing," the official said.
"Several militants are still holed up in the Special Branch section of the Kohat Police Complex," the police official told AFP on condition of anonymity.
"An exchange of fire with them has been ongoing since late last night. Their exact number remains unclear," the official added.
A statement from the Kohat district health officer late on Friday said that more than 100 people had been injured, the vast majority of them police personnel, and several were in a critical condition.
Local militant group Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a faction linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) — the Pakistani Taliban — has claimed responsibility for the attack.
AFP images showed military personnel standing by piles of bricks, rubble and blown-out walls following the attack, with soldiers carrying assault rifles guarding the complex.
Several ambulances were seen lining a street near the police compound.
Pakistan has blamed the increase in attacks in KP and the southern border province of Balochistan on militancy emanating from Afghanistan, where the Taliban government denies Afghan involvement.
The accusations have sparked a bitter rift and armed conflict between the neighbouring countries, and Pakistan has carried out deadly airstrikes it says target militants on Afghan soil.
The Taliban government in Kabul and the United Nations said dozens of civilians were killed in the latest Pakistani strikes on eastern Afghanistan in June.
Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack on Friday evening, expressing "deep sorrow and regret over the injury of several people as a result of the blast".
He directed the "best medical assistance be provided to the injured" and called for a report into the attack.
President Asif Ali Zardari expressed "regret" over the casualties, sending his "best wishes for the speedy recovery of those injured in the blast".
"The complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing is essential for national security," he said, using another term for the TTP group.
